Who Sang The Real Ghostbusters Songs? The Lost Story of Tahiti 👻📼

video // Oct 31, 2026

Watch on YouTube

I've had this Real Ghostbusters tape for, I ain't saying how long, and I just now flipped it over. 📼

"All lead vocals performed by Tahiti, featuring Tyren Perry and Tonya Townsend."

Who?

Two teenage girls sang every song on The Real Ghostbusters, and the show gave them a few seconds at the very end of the credits. My new documentary is about fixing that.

Two Ghostbusters cartoons

In the fall of 1986, there were two Ghostbusters cartoons on TV. Filmation turned its 1975 live-action kids' show, The Ghostbusters, into a cartoon. Then the studio behind the movie made one of its own, and it needed a new name: The Real Ghostbusters. Filmation's version lasted one season. The real one ran for seven.

The Real Ghostbusters premiered on ABC on September 13, 1986, and a song kicked in with episode one. Not a jingle: a full-on mid-80s pop R&B record with drums, horns and a real vocal. Every one of the 13 episodes ABC aired that fall had one.

The credit nobody saw

Watch the end credits. Producers, writers, the voice cast: Arsenio Hall, Frank Welker, Lorenzo Music. Then, for a few seconds right before the copyright, "Performed by Tahiti, featuring Tyren Perry and Tonya Townsend." Most of us had already flipped to the next cartoon.

The architect: Ollie E. Brown

Both girls thank the same man on the cassette, and they call him the same thing: my producer. Ollie E. Brown was born in Detroit, played in Stevie Wonder's band Wonderlove, and toured with the Rolling Stones on percussion. With Jerry Knight, a founding member of Ray Parker Jr.'s group Raydio, he made "Breakin'... There's No Stoppin' Us" as Ollie & Jerry. It went top 10 on the Hot 100.

For the cartoon, Ollie produced, arranged and co-wrote all 10 songs, and he's the drummer on them. All of it ran through his company, Brown Sugar Productions. Tahiti wasn't something a cartoon studio dreamed up in a meeting. It all points to Ollie.

Judy Winslow's big sister

Tyren had two little sisters, Jania and the baby, Jaimee. Y'all remember Judy Winslow, the little sister on Family Matters who went upstairs one day and never came back down? Judy was played by Jaimee Foxworth.

On the song "Movie Star," the liner notes credit the Kiddy Funk Singers: Jania Foxworth, Daralyn Phinnessee and Jaimee Foxworth. About three years before Jaimee walked into the Winslow house, all three kids were singing backup on big sister Tyren's Ghostbusters tape.

10 songs, 10 Saturdays

Every song matches its episode, and most of the titles give the case away. An electric ghost blacks out New York in "Killerwatt," and the girls answer with "Charge You Up." Slimer runs away from the firehouse, and they sing him a ballad, "Remember Home." That's 10 songs, 10 Saturdays and 10 cases, and two teenage girls are on every single one.

Who was in the room

The tape was cut at Ameraycan Studios in North Hollywood, co-owned by Ray Parker Jr., where he recorded the Ghostbusters theme. Bernie Grundman mastered it. On guitar: Paul Jackson Jr., the same Paul Jackson Jr. who played on Michael Jackson's Thriller. Gerald Albright on sax, Eric Marienthal in the horns, Gene Page on strings. And one guitar solo, on "Hometown Hero," is Ray Parker Jr. himself.

All of that, for a Saturday morning cartoon.

Then Tahiti just stopped

We couldn't find a second album, a music video, a TV performance or a magazine interview. After that first season, the record goes quiet. Then this year, Tyren talked about it in her own words: they finished the record, the show came out, and she didn't hear from Tonya again.

So the documentary goes looking: where Tyren went next (Bustin' Loose, Columbia Records, a solo album produced by Ollie Brown), the Foxworth sisters' story, and the hardest case on the tape, Tonya Townsend.

Help us find Tonya Townsend

Tonya sang every one of these songs right alongside Tyren. After Tahiti she turns up in movies like Beverly Hills Brats (1989), and in 1991 a singer credited as Tonya N. Townsend appears on an album by a trio called Once Upon a Time, with Paul Jackson Jr. on guitar. If you know Tonya, or you've got that 1991 Once Upon a Time CD booklet, tell us.

And that cassette? One copy sold on Discogs for $499.99. Go check your mama's attic.

Sources (from the video): the original 1986 Polydor cassette packaging (831 236-4), the show's own end credits, Discogs, GBFans, Spook Central, IMDb, and the artists' own interviews and pages. Where a source couldn't be confirmed, the video says so on screen.

Quick answers

Who sang the songs on The Real Ghostbusters? Tahiti, a duo of two teenage girls, Tyren Perry and Tonya Townsend, sang the songs in the show's 1986 season.

Who produced the Real Ghostbusters songs? Ollie E. Brown produced, arranged and co-wrote all 10 songs, and played drums on them.

Was Judy Winslow from Family Matters on the Real Ghostbusters soundtrack? Yes. Jaimee Foxworth, who played Judy, is credited as one of the Kiddy Funk Singers on the song "Movie Star." Her big sister is Tyren Perry of Tahiti.

Was the Real Ghostbusters soundtrack ever released on CD? We couldn't find a single documented CD. Every copy we've seen is a cassette.

Your turn

Which Tahiti song is the hardest? And if you've got any piece of this history, an old ad, a VHS with the songs or that CD that supposedly doesn't exist, tell us in the comments on the YouTube video. 👇
